MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 6, 2019
(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, February 6, 2019, in the Community
Room, on the first floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Sharon Mann-Garrett, Economic Development Manager,
the meeting was called to order at 5:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present:  Commissioner Erick Holly
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo
  Acting Chairman Terry Coleman
Excused
Absence:  Chairman Larry Spring

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Fred Jackson, Senior Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., Director of E.C.D.
  Sharon Mann-Garrett, Manager of E.D.
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Ms. Wilcox stated that Item 5a is being pulled from tonight’s PC
meeting, and will be re-noticed at a later date.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None.

(5) PUBLIC HEARING:

5A. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2018-014(SP-2018-014) AT 330 EAST
MANCHESTER BOULEVARD. A public hearing to consider an application
by Aria Shafiee, representing 330 Manchester Management LLC, for
Special Use Permit No. 2018-014 (SP-2018-014) to allow the retail
sale of beer and wine for off-site consumption in a proposed
convenience market on a 55,315 square-foot HC (Historic Core) zoned
property at 330 East Manchester Boulevard. This item has been
pulled and will be re-noticed.

5B. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2018-008 (SP-2018-008) AT 532 WEST
MANCHESTER BOULEVARD. A public hearing to consider an application
by Cole Feyijimi to appeal the denial of a Sign Adjustment No.
2018-008 (SA-2018-008) to legalize a previously installed
approximately 48 square-foot internally-illuminated bi-faced LED
sign for the display of on-site advertising only, C-2 (General
Commercial) zoned property at 532 West Manchester Boulevard.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Planner made the staff presentation.

Acting Chairman Coleman asked the Planning Commission if there
were any questions for staff.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 6, 2019
Commissioner Rice asked:
 Is there any reason the sign is not currently illuminated, nor
  has not been on since its installation as it appears to be
  operational?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that there was a mandate from Code
  Enforcement to the owner to have the sign turned off until
  the appropriate approvals are obtained.
 Have you personally had the opportunity to see the sign
  illuminated?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated no he has not.

Commissioner Trejo asked:
 What type of sign is it, an electronic sign?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated it is an electronic LED sign that would
  display general information regarding the business, also
  showing services that are provided at the subject site, as
  well as any types of listings the applicant may have for
  purchase here in the City of Inglewood or beyond.
 Was the sign installed illegally?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated yes, but to better clarify the situation,
  the applicant had a previous pole sign approved that would
  allow for a small strip LED sign to give the date,
  temperature, time of day, along with a flat-panel raceway
  pole sign above that which gave the name of the business,
  hours of operation and location. What the applicant did was
  switch the size of the signs and they’re location on the pole.
  The small LED strip which originally gave a line of text has
  now been increased in size to give a full LED Animated Display
  to show properties available for purchase as well as listings
  already sold, with services provided in large LED Lettering.
 Was it Code Enforcement that was made aware of this?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated yes, actually it was the applicant who
  once was cited by Code Enforcement, came into the City’s
  planning office to find out how he could have the new sign
  approved and obtain a permit for the sign design and layout,
  and that was when he was informed that this type of signage
  is not approved here in Inglewood and that he would have to
  apply for a Sign Adjustment. Now the actual area of the pole
  sign was not increased, just the size of the LED sign was
  increased to become larger while the flat-panel raceway sign
  became smaller, which was the catalyst that required the
  applicant to apply for the Sign Adjustment.
 So to be clear, the actual size of the sign did not increase,
  but the switching to the larger LED sign was the key?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated yes, the actual larger LED sign with
  displayed images is not allowed per the Inglewood Municipal
  Code without a sign adjustment permit and what is allowed per
  the code is electronic signs with text of time, hours of
  operation, information of services, and date.
 So if it is approved, by the display the darkened area would be
  what is being shown right now, but if it is not approved,
  although the sign size remains the same the applicant will have
  to change what is being displayed?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that the applicant will have the option
  to go back to what was originally approved and permitted,
  which was the flat-panel raceway pole sign and or they would
  just be able to only display time, temperature and date. No
  images of any sort would be allowed.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 6, 2019
Acting Chairman Coleman asked:
 When Code Enforcement went out to cite the applicant, what
  caught their attention, was the sign lit up at the time?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that although he was not made privy to
  everything that transpired or know how Code Enforcement works
  within  their  capacity,  he  believes  that
  the signage was on and of course Code Enforcement in doing
  their due diligence, asked the applicant to turn off the
  signage, because they were not able to find an authorized
  sign adjustment permit, just the old pole design signed
  with the electronic sign.
 Is the sign animated or were the images still?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated the sign was on the issue was that it was
  an LED sign that was outside of the scope of what the IMC
  allows without the sign adjustment.
 Does staff know if this application is approved, will the
  displays be animated or still?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that per the applicant who is present,
  stated that if the sign is allowed to be utilized as is, it
  will have the display of the services that the business
  provides, finance and investments, current and past listings
  along with pictures of the listings from all over, not just
  Inglewood.
 Per the agenda packet, the applicant submitted a letter stating
  that an “eight-wheeled” vehicle parked would be large enough to
  block the sign as well as his business and he believes that the
  applicant is speaking about an “eighteen-wheeler” truck and was
  he correct in his summation of the applicant’s letter?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated yes that is correct, the applicant was
  meaning to say “eighteen wheeler”.

Commissioner Holly asked:
 If what the applicant is proposing similar to what is already
  displayed across town last year with another applicant in the
  City?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that although he is not aware of the other
  signage, this applicant is wanting to advertise other
  properties that are for sale which are not listed only in
  Inglewood, which would make the sign a completely different
  type of signage display that is not allowed per the IMC.

Commissioner Rice asked:
 In looking at the permit that was issued in May 2003 for the
  sign and that it should be a 6x9 Can, pole, with red neon
  borders, and excavation, which is a pole in the ground and also
  non-illuminated. Do you know if at any time the applicant
  changed the sign to show time, date and temperature?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that if in fact it was not approved under
  the original signage, then that would be a requirement.

Acting Chairman Coleman asked for the applicant to come forward
and address the planning commission.

Mr. Cole Feyijimi, owner made his presentation  and  answered
questions from the planning commission.

Commissioner Holly asked:
 Mr. Feyijimi, we would like to know why you did not do your due
  diligence and contact the planning division when you decided to
  change your original sign?
  - Mr. Feyijimi stated that he wasn’t sure what he was supposed
  to do with regards to obtaining a sign adjustment permit,
  since he had already received a sign permit in 2003. He felt

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 6, 2019
  it was not necessary to obtain another permit since he already
  had the permit from 2003. The pole sign was already approved.

Commissioner Rice asked:
 Mr. Feyijimi, when and how did an eighteen wheeler block the
  pole sign and your business from being seen, when as high as
  the pole sign is, that seems a bit doubtful.
  - Mr. Feyijimi stated it is a true statement. One weekend, there
  was a driver who was staying at the hotel across the street
  and left his truck on our side of the street for the entire
  weekend, blocking our business with his truck.
 Mr. Feyijimi, who installed your pole sign without getting
  permits from the City?
  - Mr. Feyijimi stated that an acquaintance of his, knew a man
  who could make the sign, and so he contacted him. That
  gentleman made the pole sign back in 2003. So, when he made
  the decision to upgrade the sign, due to falling sales and
  trying to keep his business name present.
 Mr. Feyijimi, did you utilize a licensed contractor, was your
  associate’s friend a licensed contractor?
  - Mr. Feyijimi stated no, he did not have a license.
 Mr. Feyijimi, with your associate’s friend not having a license,
  this is what has brought you to this point, where you have a
  pole sign that cannot be approved due to the Municipal Code
  regulations.

Commissioner Trejo stated:
 Many days and evenings as she travels up and down Manchester
  Boulevard, she sees the pole sign from both near and far. The
  municipal code is in place for a reason.

Acting Chairman Coleman stated:
 He too has driven down Manchester Boulevard and immediately
  could see the pole sign from both near and far, and feels that
  it would be next to impossible to cover up the sign with an
  eighteen-wheeler.
 Mr. Feyijimi, before you were asked by Code Enforcement to
  darken your sign, was the pictures generated animated or still
  shots?
  - Mr. Feyijimi stated that the screen was animated.

Commissioner Rice asked staff:
 If Mr. Feyijimi returns the sign back to the original 2003
  approved pole sign, will he be able to utilize that for his
  sign?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that per the municipal code only what is
  approved is an illuminated sign that gives the date, time and
  hours of operation.

Acting Chairman Coleman opened the floor to the public to speak to
the planning commission for or against this item.

FOR:

Stuart Bailey, Inglewood Resident
  - Just a concerned citizen, but all is well.

AGAINST:

None

Acting-Chair Coleman asked for closing comments and also a motion
from the Planning Commission.

  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 6, 2019

MOTION:

Commissioner Trejo made the motion to affirm the notice of
exemption EA-CE-2018-099 and adopt the attached resolution
upholding the director’s denial of SA-2018-008 and was second by
Commissioner Rice, Resolution No. 1828,

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA,
  UPHOLDING THE DENIAL OF A CERTAIN SIGN
  ADJUSTMENT REQUEST TO LEGALIZE A PREVIOUSLY
  INSTALLED  APPROXIMATELY  48  SQUARE-FOOT
  INTERNALLY-ILLUMINATED BI-FACED LED SIGN FOR
  THE DISPLAY OF ON-SITE ADVERTISING ONLY ON
  APPROXIMATELY 3,700 SQUARE-FOOT C-2 (GENERAL
  COMMERCIAL) ZONED PROPERTY AT 532 WEST
  MANCHESTER BOULEVARD.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners  Holly,  Rice,  Trejo,  and  Acting-Chair
  Coleman.

Ms. Wilcox explained there is no appeals process.

(6)  COMMISSION INITIATIVES:

Commissioner Holly no initiatives,  just  wanted  to  thank  the
community for coming out.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff about any update regarding the Hotel
Parking situation at the corner of Rosewood and Century Boulevard.
  - Ms. Wilcox stated she will have a response at next month’s
  planning commission meeting.

Acting-Chair Coleman asked staff about Michael Koper situation,
  - Ms. Wilcox stated she will have a response at next month’s
  planning commission meeting.

  - Concern of lack of parking in the City.

Ms. Sharon Mann-Garrett, Manager of Economic Development Division
  - Introduced herself to the Planning Commission and the
  community.
  - Explained her position with the community and here at the
  City.
